page: Microsoft Azure D48ls_v6 is a compute-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Dlsv6 server family. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The instance features 48 dedicated vCPUs derived from 24 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It is equipped with 96.0 GB of system memory, yielding a low memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The processor includes a 260 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets, including Intel Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for accelerated matrix operations.

This server type is deployed on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It does not include any local storage, requiring the attachment of external Premium Storage volumes for persistent data. The primary hardware tradeoff of the D48ls_v6 is its low memory allocation relative to its high compute capacity, which makes it less suitable for memory-intensive workloads but highly cost-efficient for compute-heavy tasks that do not require large memory footprints.

Benchmark data indicates strong performance across several compute and memory bandwidth metrics. The instance achieves top-tier results in Geekbench image processing and strong ratings in multi-core Geekbench, Passmark CPU, and software compilation tests. Memory bandwidth tests for both small and large blocks also rank in the top 25 percent. Additionally, the hardware-assisted AMX instructions support strong performance in LLM inference for small and medium models. This profile makes the D48ls_v6 suitable for compute-bound workloads such as software compilation, image processing, web serving, and lightweight machine learning inference.
